Home → About RRWO
About Rasira Rwanda Women Organization

A survivor-founded, victim-led grassroots organization working in rural Rwanda to end stigma, discrimination, and gender-based violence — one community at a time.

Our story
Born from silence — built by survivors

In many rural communities of Rwanda, cultural myths, traditional gender roles, religious interpretations, and societal expectations create barriers for women and LBTGNC persons. Harmful narratives often label sexual and gender minorities as abnormal, sinful, or cursed — leading to rejection, family violence, forced marriages, economic exclusion, and public humiliation.

RRWO was formed in 2023 by survivors who refused to remain silent. These women and girls created safe spaces where affected persons can heal, organize, and advocate — not as victims waiting for help, but as leaders driving their own transformation.

Community members at RRWO outreach activities · Rwanda, 2025

Vision
"A rural Rwanda where every woman and LBTGNC person lives free from violence, stigma, and discrimination."
Mission
"To empower victimized women and LBTGNC persons in rural Rwanda through advocacy, community dialogue, protection services, and socio-economic strengthening."

Challenges we address
The reality we work to change
🛡️
Gender-Based Violence (GBV) including domestic violence and corrective abuse against LBTGNC persons
🕊️
Religious and cultural stigma rooted in myths and misinformation about gender and sexuality
💼
Economic marginalization and poverty disproportionately affecting women and LBTGNC persons
🏠
Family rejection and social isolation, including forced marriages and exclusion from community life
⚖️
Limited access to justice, legal protection, and support services in rural districts
Our people
Organizational structure

RRWO is led entirely by volunteers — women from the communities we serve.

C
Coordinator
Leads overall strategy, partnerships, and represents RRWO in external engagements.
P
Program Focal Person
Designs and oversees all programs, tracks activities and community outcomes.
M
Community Mobilizers
Engage villages, identify beneficiaries, and coordinate outreach activities on the ground.
P
Peer Support Leaders
Survivors who facilitate healing circles and provide psychosocial support to peers.
Where we work
Operational areas

RRWO currently operates across three districts in Rwanda, bringing programs directly to rural communities.

Kirehe
Eastern Province
Nyabihu
Western Province
Rulindo
Northern Province
Registration status
RRWO is currently a non-registered, non-profit grassroots organization. We are actively pursuing formal registration, expanded partnerships, and funding to strengthen and scale our work across Rwanda.
Home → Activities
Our work on the ground

RRWO is in its founding phase — and our volunteer team is already active, running outreach, supporting women in need, and building trust across our three districts.

🌱
We are in our founding phase. While we pursue formal registration and funding, our volunteer community mobilizers are already doing meaningful work across Kirehe, Nyabihu, and Rulindo.
What we are doing now
Current activities

Everything below is happening right now, run by our volunteer team on the ground.

01
Community resource mobilization
Ongoing
RRWO mobilizes contributions from community members — goods, food, skills, and small financial contributions — to create a shared pool of support for the most vulnerable women and girls.
Identifying women in urgent need within communities
Organizing community members to contribute what they can
Distributing support to GBV survivors and economically excluded women
Building a culture of collective care and mutual aid
02
Community outreach & women's support visits
Ongoing
Our mobilizers go directly into villages to reach women who cannot easily access services — listening, providing basic support, and connecting them to available resources.
Home and community visits to isolated women and GBV survivors
Peer-to-peer listening and emotional support sessions
Information sharing on rights, services, and protection
Referrals to local health, legal, and protection services

Community outreach sessions · Rwanda, 2025

03
Awareness dialogues on GBV & stigma
Ongoing
Through community conversations, RRWO challenges harmful cultural narratives around women and LBTGNC persons, engaging local leaders, families, and faith actors in honest dialogue.
Village dialogues with community and religious leaders
Awareness sessions on GBV, consent, and women's rights
Challenging myths and misinformation about LBTGNC identities
04
Safe space & peer healing circles
Ongoing
Survivor-led gatherings where women and LBTGNC persons can speak freely, share experiences, and support each other in a confidential environment.
Regular healing circles in all three operational districts
Confidential peer support for trauma and GBV survivors
Building trust and solidarity among members

RRWO community programs · 2025
